items.title: Vowel Leap Progression
items.prompt: Determine the rule governing this sequence of letter pairs and identify the next term.
items.hint: Track the alphabetical positions of both the first and second letter independently.
items.explanation: The first letter advances by increasing increments (+2, +3, +4, +5), moving from J (10) to O (15), while the second letter steps backward by 1 alphabetically (Z, Y, X, W, V).

items.title: The Weightless Burden
items.prompt: The more you take away from me, the larger I become. What am I?
items.hint: Think about what remains in the ground when you dig.
items.explanation: A hole expands in physical size precisely as material is removed from it.

items.title: Peninsular Outlier
items.prompt: Which of these world capitals does not share the distinct geographical classification of the other three?
items.hint: Consider which nations are completely surrounded by water versus attached to a continent.
items.explanation: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal on mainland Europe, whereas Reykjavik, Tokyo, and Wellington are capitals of island nations.

items.title: Cloud Weight Reality
items.prompt: Fact or Myth: A typical cumulus cloud weighs as much as hundreds of thousands of kilograms (over 1 million pounds).
items.hint: Consider the vast volume of tiny suspended water droplets.
items.explanation: An average cumulus cloud spans roughly one cubic kilometer with a droplet density that totals approximately 500,000 kilograms (1.1 million pounds). It stays aloft because its massive weight is dispersed across a huge volume less dense than surrounding dry air.

items.title: Missing Corner Dot
items.prompt: Each block contains a colored circle and an internal numeric counter. What number completes the bottom-right block according to the established visual rule?

svgDiagram.caption: Grid of sized nodes with value counters

items.hint: Examine how circle radius and position relate to the value in each block.
items.explanation: Each block's number equals the circle radius multiplied by its column index (left column = 1, right column = 2). The bottom-right circle has radius 16, so 16 × 2 = 32.

items.title: Server Bay Assignment
items.prompt: Four distinct servers (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta) are installed in consecutive rack bays numbered 1 to 4 from top to bottom. Identify which server occupies Bay 2.
clues: 1. Beta is placed directly below Alpha.
2. Gamma is not in Bay 1 and not in Bay 4.
3. Delta is placed in a higher bay number than Gamma.
items.hint: Start with Gamma's restricted position and work outward.
items.explanation: Gamma cannot be in Bay 1 or 4, so Gamma is in Bay 2 or 3. Because Delta is below Gamma, and Alpha-Beta must occupy adjacent slots, Alpha and Beta take Bays 1 and 2, Gamma takes Bay 3, and Delta takes Bay 4.

items.title: Cosmic Departure Ladder
items.prompt: Arrange these celestial bodies in ascending order of their surface escape velocity (from lowest to highest).
items.hint: Smaller, less massive worlds generally require less speed to escape their gravitational pull.
items.explanation: The Moon has an escape velocity of about 2.4 km/s, Mars is roughly 5.0 km/s, Earth is 11.2 km/s, and Jupiter is the highest at nearly 60 km/s.

items.title: Subsea Sensor Balancing
items.prompt: Select exactly 3 deep-sea monitoring nodes whose depth ratings sum up to 100 meters.
items.hint: Two of the required numbers end in 5.
items.explanation: Selecting 15, 35, and 50 yields exactly 100 meters, meeting the depth balance requirement.

items.title: The Unbroken Vessel
items.prompt: I can be cracked without ever being struck, and I can be made without any tools. Once told, I am often shared, but if taken too far, I hurt. What am I?
items.hint: Think about something you might tell at a party.
items.explanation: A joke can be 'cracked', made up, and told to others, but can hurt if taken too far.

items.title: The Weightless Vessel
items.prompt: I can fill an entire room without taking up any space, and the more of me you add, the lighter the room feels. What am I?
items.hint: Flip a switch to invite me in.
items.explanation: Light permeates a room completely without displacing any physical matter or adding weight, brightening the space instantly.

items.title: Observatory Shift Roster
items.prompt: Four astronomers (Aria, Blake, Chen, and Dev) each monitored a different telescope: Optical, Radio, Infrared, or X-ray. Who operated the Infrared telescope?
clues: 1. Aria and Dev operated non-optical telescopes that detect longer wavelengths than visible light.
2. Chen operated the X-ray telescope.
3. Aria did not operate the Radio telescope.
items.hint: Infrared and Radio are both longer in wavelength than visible light.
items.explanation: Because Aria and Dev operated longer-wavelength instruments (Radio and Infrared) and Aria did not use the Radio telescope, Aria must have operated the Infrared telescope.

items.title: Monarchic Terminations
items.prompt: Which of these European monarchs is the odd one out regarding how their reign ended?
items.hint: Consider whether each monarch lost their life or voluntarily gave up power.
options: Edward VIII of the United Kingdom
items.explanation: Edward VIII voluntarily abdicated his throne in 1936, whereas Charles I, Louis XVI, and Nicholas II were all executed during revolutions.

items.title: Glass in Ancient Cathedrals
items.prompt: Antique stained-glass windows in medieval European cathedrals are noticeably thicker at the base because glass is an ultra-slow liquid that has sagged downward over hundreds of years.
items.hint: Consider the medieval manufacturing techniques used by glassblowers.
items.explanation: Glass is an amorphous solid, not a slow-flowing liquid at room temperature. Medieval window panes vary in thickness because artisans created sheets by spinning molten glass into cylinders or discs and naturally installed the heavier, thicker edges at the bottom for structural stability.

items.title: Symmetric Balance Point
items.prompt: Examine the three numbered balance arms displayed in the diagram. Which value correctly replaces the question mark (?) to keep the right arm in equilibrium?

svgDiagram.caption: Torque balance arms with distances and masses

items.hint: Calculate the product of weight and distance from the central fulcrum for each arm.
items.explanation: In balance arms 1 and 2, the left and right moments match: 6 × 4 = 8 × 3 (24) and 5 × 6 = 10 × 3 (30). For arm 3, the left moment is 4 × 9 = 36, so the right side needs ? × 6 = 36, which yields 6.

items.title: Cryogenic Cell Matrix
items.prompt: Select exactly 3 cells whose thermal unit values sum to exactly 50 to stabilize the core.

gridPuzzle.instruction: Select exactly 3 cells that sum to 50.

items.hint: Try combining one large value in the twenties with two smaller compatible values.
items.explanation: Selecting cells with values 27, 15, and 8 gives 27 + 15 + 8 = 50, successfully meeting the target sum with exactly 3 cells.

items.title: Noble Gas Disrupter
items.prompt: Which of these chemical elements does not belong with the others?
items.hint: Consider their periodic table group classification.
items.explanation: Argon, Neon, and Krypton are inert noble gases found in Group 18 of the periodic table, whereas Nitrogen is a diatomic nonmetal in Group 15.

items.title: Chronology of Communication
items.prompt: Arrange these groundbreaking communication technologies in chronological order of their invention/introduction, from earliest to latest.
items.hint: Electric telegraph came before the acoustic telephone.
items.explanation: The electric telegraph emerged in the 1830s-1840s, Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876, Marconi demonstrated practical radio in 1895, and ARPANET debuted in 1969.

items.title: Cubic Prime Shift
items.prompt: Identify the logical pattern governing the sequence and determine the missing final number.
items.hint: Consider the relationship between consecutive cubes (n^3) and small integer adjustments.

items.title: Concentric Sector Split
items.prompt: Each ring is divided into equal angular sectors. What total fraction of the outer ring is shaded in dark blue?
items.hint: Count the total number of divisions in the outermost perimeter.
items.explanation: The outer ring is divided into 6 equal angular sectors, exactly 2 of which are filled with dark blue. Simplifying 2/6 yields 1/3.

items.title: The Borrowed Breath
items.prompt: I can be cracked, made, told, and played, yet I possess neither voice nor physical form. What am I?
items.hint: You might hear one at a comedy club.
items.explanation: A joke can be cracked, made, told, or played on someone, despite having no physical body or independent voice.

items.title: Orbital Pod Allocation
items.prompt: Four astronauts (Aria, Blake, Chen, and Devi) occupy consecutive docking bays numbered 1 through 4. Determine who is assigned to Bay 3 using the clues below.
clues: 1. Devi's bay has a higher number than all the others.
2. Aria's bay is directly adjacent to Blake's bay.
3. Blake is not assigned to Bay 1 or Bay 4.
4. Chen does not occupy Bay 1.
items.hint: Start with Blake's position relative to the end bays.
items.explanation: Devi is in Bay 4 because she has the highest number. Aria and Blake are adjacent, and Blake is not at an end, placing Blake in Bay 2 and Aria in Bay 1, leaving Chen in Bay 3.

items.title: Sunken Buoyancy
items.prompt: Because water pressure increases dramatically with ocean depth, a solid steel ball dropped over the Mariana Trench will eventually stop sinking and float suspended in the water.
items.hint: Consider the relative compressibility of liquid water compared to the density of solid steel.
items.explanation: Water is nearly incompressible, so its density increases by only a few percent at the bottom of the trench, remaining far below the density of steel (~7.8 g/cm³ versus ~1.08 g/cm³). Thus, the steel ball sinks all the way to the ocean floor.

items.title: Substation Power Surge
items.prompt: Select exactly 3 transformer cells that together deliver a total output of 50 megawatts.
items.hint: Identify three numbers that end with digits summing to a multiple of 10.
items.explanation: Selecting 12, 19, and 19 sums to 50 (12 + 19 + 19 = 50).

items.title: Planetary Daybreak
items.prompt: Three of these Solar System planets rotate on their axes in a prograde (counterclockwise) direction, while one rotates retrograde. Which is the odd one out?
items.hint: On this world, the Sun appears to rise in the west and set in the east.
items.explanation: Venus rotates clockwise (retrograde) relative to Earth, Mars, and Neptune, which all spin prograde.

items.title: Chronicles of Flight
items.prompt: Arrange these historic aviation and space milestones in chronological order from earliest to latest.
orderItems: Wright brothers' powered flight at Kitty Hawk
items.hint: Balloons preceded heavier-than-air powered flight by over a century.
items.explanation: The Montgolfier balloon flew in 1783, the Wright brothers took off in 1903, the sound barrier was broken in 1947, and Apollo 11 landed in 1969.

items.title: Prime Gap Multipliers
items.prompt: Find the missing number in the sequence based on the underlying progression rule.
items.hint: Look at the differences between consecutive terms: +3, +5, +7, +11...
items.explanation: The differences added to each step are consecutive prime numbers: +3, +5, +7, +11, and +13. Adding 13 to 28 yields 41.

items.title: Solar Array Calibration
items.prompt: Select exactly 3 solar cells whose power ratings sum to exactly 50 kW.
items.hint: Try pairing the highest value with two smaller values.
items.explanation: Selecting cells with ratings 27, 15, and 8 gives 27 + 15 + 8 = 50 kW.

items.title: The Silent Traveler
items.prompt: I can travel around the entire world while staying confined in my single corner. What am I?
items.hint: You attach me to letters before sending them away.
items.explanation: A postage stamp is affixed to the corner of an envelope and journeys worldwide without ever moving from that spot.

items.title: Archival Storage Protocol
items.prompt: Four mineral samples (Beryl, Quartz, Topaz, Zircon) are placed into lockers 1, 2, 3, and 4 in a row. Determine which mineral sits in Locker 3.
clues: Beryl occupies Locker 1.
Quartz is placed immediately adjacent to Beryl.
Topaz occupies a higher-numbered locker than Quartz, but is not directly next to Quartz.
items.hint: Place Beryl and Quartz first using clues 1 and 2.
items.explanation: Beryl is in locker 1, Quartz in locker 2 (next to Beryl), Topaz in locker 4 (higher than Quartz and not adjacent to it), leaving Zircon in locker 3.

items.title: Square Factor Cadence
items.prompt: Determine the next number in this sequence based on the underlying progression.
items.hint: Consider the number of positive divisors for sequential integers.
items.explanation: The sequence counts the number of positive divisors for consecutive integers starting from 1: d(1)=1, d(2)=2... wait, for 1, 4, 9: d(1)=1, d(4)=3, d(6)=4. Rather, integers 1 through 6 have divisor counts: d(1)=1, d(2)=2, d(3)=2, d(4)=3, d(5)=2, d(6)=4.

items.title: Chameleon Camouflage Intent
items.prompt: Fact or Myth: Chameleons primarily change their skin color to blend in with their background surroundings.
items.hint: Think about how reptiles communicate and regulate internal conditions.
items.explanation: Chameleons alter their skin color mainly for thermoregulation and social communication, such as signaling aggression or territory, rather than active background camouflage.

items.title: Equilateral Wedge Balance
items.prompt: A regular hexagon is subdivided into six equal equilateral triangles. If three alternating triangles are colored dark teal and the remaining three are divided in half, what percentage of the hexagon's total area is dark teal?

svgDiagram.caption: Regular hexagon divided into alternating shaded sections

items.hint: Count the fraction of full equilateral triangles filled with teal.
items.explanation: Exactly three out of the six identical equilateral triangles forming the hexagon are shaded dark teal, which equals 3/6 or 50% of the total area.

items.title: The Cipher Key Assignment
items.prompt: Four cryptographers—Anya, Ben, Clara, and David—each safeguard exactly one unique security key: Amber, Cobalt, Jade, or Ruby. Determine who holds the Cobalt key based on these findings.
clues: 1. Neither Anya nor David holds the Jade key.
2. Clara holds the Ruby key.
3. Ben does not hold the Amber key or the Cobalt key.
items.hint: Start by identifying who must hold the Jade key.
items.explanation: Since Clara holds Ruby, Ben cannot hold Amber or Cobalt, leaving Ben with Jade. Anya cannot hold Jade, so Anya and David hold Amber and Cobalt; with David excluded from Jade and Ben holding Jade, Anya holds Cobalt and David holds Amber.

items.title: Glandular Oddity
items.prompt: Which of these biological glands differs fundamentally from the other three in how it releases its secretions?
items.hint: Consider whether secretions enter ducts or travel directly into the bloodstream.
items.explanation: The salivary gland is an exocrine gland that secretes through specialized ducts, whereas the thyroid, pituitary, and adrenal are endocrine glands secreting hormones directly into the bloodstream.

items.title: Printed Epochs
items.prompt: Arrange these communication technologies in chronological order of their historical invention or introduction, from earliest to most recent.
items.hint: Woodblock printing originated centuries before European movable metal type.
items.explanation: Woodblock printing emerged first (circa 7th-8th century), followed by Gutenberg's movable type press (c. 1440), the rotary printing press (1843), and Samuel Morse's commercial telegraph rollout (1844).

items.title: Gear Teeth Match
items.prompt: If Gear A rotates clockwise, in which direction will Gear D rotate, and how many gears turn counter-clockwise in total?

svgDiagram.caption: A train of four interlocked gears in sequence

items.hint: Adjacent meshed gears always rotate in opposite directions.
items.explanation: Meshed gears alternate rotation directions: A is clockwise, B counter-clockwise, C clockwise, and D counter-clockwise. Thus, Gear D rotates counter-clockwise and exactly two gears turn counter-clockwise.

items.title: Grid Voltage Calibration
items.prompt: Select exactly 3 cells whose values sum to 50 to stabilize the circuit voltage.

gridPuzzle.instruction: Select exactly 3 cells that sum to 50.

items.hint: Look for a combination of two values in the teens and twenties that bridge to 50.
items.explanation: Selecting 11, 15, and 24 yields a sum of exactly 50 (11 + 15 + 24 = 50).

items.title: The Vanishing Footprint
items.prompt: The more you take from me, the more you leave behind. What am I?
items.hint: Think about walking along a sandy beach.
items.explanation: Every step you take leaves a footprint behind in your path.

items.title: Cosmic Distance Ladder
items.prompt: Arrange these celestial bodies in order of their average distance from Earth, from closest to farthest.
items.hint: Start with our own natural satellite and work your way out.
items.explanation: The Moon is closest (~384,400 km), followed by Mars (~225 million km average), the Sun (~150 million km at closest, though Mars's closest approach is nearer than the Sun), and finally Proxima Centauri (~4.24 light-years away).

items.title: Roman Century Steps
items.prompt: Determine the rule governing the sequence of Roman numerals and find the next entry.
items.hint: Convert each numeral to Arabic numbers and look for the growing increment.
items.explanation: The Roman numerals represent perfect squares: 1 (1²), 4 (2²), 9 (3²), and 16 (4²). The next square is 25 (5²), which is written as XXV.

items.title: The Great Wall Visibility
items.prompt: Fact or Myth: The Great Wall of China is easily visible to the naked human eye from low Earth orbit without any magnification.
items.hint: Consider the wall's width compared to human optical resolution from orbit.
items.explanation: Astronauts and NASA confirm the Great Wall is generally not visible to the unaided eye from orbit because it is narrow and blends with natural terrain.

items.title: Aviation Milestones
items.prompt: Arrange these historic aviation milestones in chronological order, from earliest to most recent.
orderItems: First supersonic flight by Chuck Yeager
Wright Brothers' first powered flight at Kitty Hawk
Maiden commercial flight of the Boeing 747
items.hint: Consider the transition from piston-driven flight to jet-powered travel.
items.explanation: The Wright brothers flew in 1903, Lindbergh crossed the Atlantic solo in 1927, Chuck Yeager broke the sound barrier in 1947, and the Boeing 747 entered commercial service in 1970.

items.title: Alphanumeric Progression
items.prompt: Find the missing term that completes this alphanumeric pattern.
items.hint: Track the letter advancing forward and the number doubling.
items.explanation: Letters advance by consecutive increments (+1, +2, +3, +4) while numbers double each step (3, 6, 12, 24, 48). Moving 4 steps past G gives K, paired with 48.

items.title: Glass Fluidity Fallacy
items.prompt: Fact Check: Medieval stained glass windows are thicker at the bottom because glass is a slow-flowing liquid at room temperature.
items.hint: Think about how medieval artisans manufactured crown and cylinder glass.
items.explanation: Glass is an amorphous solid that does not flow noticeably at ambient temperatures. Medieval panes are uneven due to ancient manufacturing techniques, and builders simply placed the thicker edge at the base for structural stability.

items.title: Angle of the Golden Ratio
items.prompt: Examine the segmented circle diagram. What is the value of angle theta in degrees?

svgDiagram.caption: Segmented circle showing known angles and unknown angle theta

items.hint: The circle is divided into three sections; sum the known angles and subtract from 360 degrees.
items.explanation: A complete circle measures 360 degrees. Subtracting 150 degrees and 125 degrees leaves exactly 85 degrees for theta.

items.title: Quantum Reactor Cells
items.prompt: Select exactly 3 power cells that combine to reach a total output of 50 megawatts.

gridPuzzle.instruction: Select exactly 3 cells that sum to 50

items.hint: Look for two large double-digit numbers that leave an easy remainder.
items.explanation: Selecting 23, 19, and 8 gives 23 + 19 + 8 = 50 megawatts.

items.title: The Weightless Pocket
items.prompt: I can fill an entire room without occupying any physical space, and the more of me you take away, the darker things become. What am I?
items.hint: Switch me on when evening falls.
items.explanation: Light fills a room completely without displacing any physical mass or volume.

items.title: The Diplomatic Summit
items.prompt: Four ambassadors (A, B, C, D) sit in a row facing north. Deduce who sits in the third position from the left.
clues: 1. Ambassador D sits on one of the extreme ends.
2. Ambassador B sits exactly one seat to the right of Ambassador C.
3. Ambassador A is not sitting next to Ambassador C.
4. Ambassador D sits to the right of Ambassador A.
items.hint: Place D at the extreme end first, then position B and C.
items.explanation: D must sit on an extreme end; placing D at seat 4 allows B at seat 2 and C immediately to B's left at seat 1, leaving seat 3 for A.
